canonical_definition: Based on the provided data, Professionalism is defined as a latent attribute of pre-training text, indicating the extent to which it contains professional knowledge. One paper specifies this knowledge as the type found in "textbooks or research articles" and frames it as a dimension that "serves as an indicator of the level of professional knowledge contained in the text" ("Meta-rater: A Multi-dimensional Data Selection Method for Pre-training Language Models"). This work also suggests that Professionalism supports advanced model capabilities in knowledge-intensive tasks. A separate paper proposes a causal relationship where human preference alignment is reported to cause Professionalism. The provided materials do not contain information on how this construct is operationalized or measured.
expert_removed_reason: data property/engineering: a quality dimension of pre-training text used for data selection, not a property of the model
